scope: 3.1. Organic removal efficiency in AnMBR systems

matched: Consistent AnMBR performance across all operational stages despite variations in HRT and OLR
Start-up and adaptation phase (days 1-28): Influent COD increased while HRT decreased from 15 to 9.5 days
Start-up phase COD removal rising from 90% to 99%, effluent COD < 900 mg/L, OLR increased from 0.42 to 4.65 kg/m3.d
Stable operation phase (days 29-103): HRT reduced to 6.5 days with 100% raw leachate, robust and stable performance approaching treatment capacity
Shock loading phase (days 104-120): OLR 7.5 to 8.0 kg COD/m3.d, effluent COD peaked at ~5500 mg/L, COD removal dropped to 84-88% due to organic overload and toxicity
Effluent NH4+-N persistently high averaging 1300 mg/L throughout experiment (Fig. 1b)
Limited capacity of AnMBR for NH4+-N removal under strictly anaerobic conditions despite high organic removal
Integration of AnMBR with aerobic post-treatment (nitrification or partial nitritation) recommended to enhance nitrogen removal
